Multilevel Random-Intercept Prediction-Powered Inference (ppi_lmer)

Source: R/ppi_clustered.R
ppi_lmer.Rd

Combines a multilevel random-intercept linear mixed model (lme4::lmer) with Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI / PPI++). Accepts either an lme4-style random-intercept formula (y ~ x1 + x2 + (1 | cluster)) or a fixed-effects formula (y ~ x1 + x2) plus cluster. Estimates variance components (\(\tau^2\), \(\sigma^2\), ICC) via REML on the human-validated set, forms exact Woodbury random-intercept GLS weights (when clusters are disjoint across labeled and unlabeled sets, or total-cluster inverse-variance weights when clusters overlap, preserving exact unbiasedness under arbitrary LLM bias), and computes cluster-robust PPI++ sandwich standard errors alongside human-only and naive-LLM multilevel benchmarks.

Usage

ppi_lmer(
  formula,
  data,
  pred_col,
  cluster = NULL,
  unlabeled = NULL,
  method = c("ppi++", "ppi"),
  lambda = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  weight_mode = c("gls", "ols"),
  small_sample_df = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

Either a random-intercept formula y ~ x1 + x2 + (1 | grp) or a fixed-effects formula y ~ x1 + x2 paired with cluster.

data

A data.frame containing response, covariates, pred_col, and cluster IDs. When unlabeled = NULL, rows with missing response form the unlabeled set.

pred_col

Name of the LLM-coded outcome column.

cluster

Optional cluster column name (inferred from (1 | cluster) in formula if omitted).

unlabeled

Optional separate data.frame of unlabeled observations.

method

"ppi++" (default) or "ppi" (lambda = 1).

lambda

Optional numeric override for lambda in [0, 1].

conf_level

Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.

weight_mode

"gls" (default, REML random-intercept GLS weighting) or "ols" (unweighted cluster-robust PPI++).

small_sample_df

Logical; use \(t\) degrees of freedom based on effective cluster count. Default TRUE.

Value

An S3 object of class c("llm_ppi_lmer", "llm_ppi_clustered", "llm_ppi") with $variance_components (human vs. naive-LLM \(\tau^2\), \(\sigma^2\), ICC) in addition to standard llm_ppi components.

Examples

set.seed(11)
G <- 50
m <- 5
cid <- rep(paste0("p", seq_len(G)), each = m)
u <- rep(rnorm(G, sd = 0.9), each = m)
x <- rnorm(G * m)
y_true <- 2.0 + 1.0 * x + u + rnorm(G * m, sd = 0.6)
y_llm <- 0.4 + 0.8 * y_true + rnorm(G * m, sd = 0.5)
df <- tibble::tibble(
  person = cid,
  x = x,
  human_y = ifelse(cid %in% paste0("p", 1:20), y_true, NA_real_),
  llm_y = y_llm
)
fit <- ppi_lmer(human_y ~ x + (1 | person), data = df, pred_col = "llm_y")
fit
#> 
#> ── Prediction-Powered Inference (ppi++_lmer) 
#> Labeled n = 100 | Unlabeled N = 150 | lambda = 0.535 | CI = 95%
#> Clusters (person): 20 labeled, 30 unlabeled (50 total; disjoint)
#> Random-intercept REML (human): tau2 = 0.526, sigma2 = 0.371, ICC = 0.586 |
#> Weighting: gls_woodbury
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   term        estimate std_error conf_low conf_high p_value var_gain
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)    1.75     0.117     1.51       2.00 <0.0001     2.17
#> 2 x              0.991    0.0595    0.866      1.12 <0.0001     0.74
